Description: Unique identifier for the application
Informs design decision: Traceability from finding to design decision
Caveats: Register records intent, not behaviour

Description: Business name and purpose
Informs design decision: Scoping and stakeholder communication
Caveats: Names differ between tools; keep an alias list

Description: Person accountable for the application
Informs design decision: Who approves the target hosting model
Secondary or cross-check source: App owner confirmation; vSphere notes or tags
Caveats: Often missing or stale

Description: Who supports and changes the application
Informs design decision: Who validates the design and runs migration testing
Caveats: Confirm per application

Description: Identity of installed software
Informs design decision: Vendor support for relocation; version exceptions
Secondary or cross-check source: Aria Service Discovery (Type, Version); Application Inventory
Caveats: Onboarded devices only

Description: Whether the software or OS is past vendor support
Informs design decision: Exception list: unsupported software that cannot move as-is
Caveats: Onboarded devices only

Description: COTS, bespoke, SaaS, appliance or file service
Informs design decision: Which archetype the application belongs to
Source detail: From Defender software inventory and hosting platform (HST-08)
Caveats: Confirm bespoke applications with the owner

Description: Business criticality and tolerable outage
Informs design decision: Hub resilience and failover design
Source detail: Business continuity plans or owner statement
Caveats: No tool can observe this

Description: Fully qualified hostname
Informs design decision: Join key across tools
Caveats: Renames and short names break joins; prefer UUID or MAC

Description: VMware identifiers for the VM
Informs design decision: Joins VM inventory to discovered services
Source detail: vCenter FQDN plus VM managed object ID
Caveats: MOID is unique only within one vCenter

Description: Hardware UUID of the VM
Informs design decision: Reliable join between VMware and Defender
Caveats: Byte order of the first three groups may differ between sources; test on a sample

Description: Every IP assigned to the host
Informs design decision: Join to network logs and IPAM
Caveats: IPs change; record the observation date

Description: MAC address of each NIC
Informs design decision: Join between VMware, Defender and RunZero
Caveats: Keep each MAC aligned with its IPs and port group

Description: Physical site hosting the component
Informs design decision: Which hub each workload moves to
Secondary or cross-check source: VMware datacenter or cluster; RunZero site
Caveats: Accurate only where prefixes are assigned to sites; flag unmatched IPs

Description: Country and region of the hosting site
Informs design decision: Regional hub assignment; data residency checks
Caveats: None

Description: VM, physical server, appliance, cloud or SaaS
Informs design decision: Archetype and migration method
Source detail: VMware inventory; RunZero asset type and hardware fingerprint
Caveats: Standalone ESXi hosts and non-VMware hypervisors are visible only to RunZero

Description: Where the VM runs in vSphere
Informs design decision: Hub capacity grouping; co-located workloads
Caveats: VMs on hosts outside vCenter are missing

Description: Guest OS, version and distribution
Informs design decision: Legacy OS exceptions; target platform compatibility
Secondary or cross-check source: VMware guest OS; RunZero OS fingerprint
Caveats: Use VMware or RunZero for devices not onboarded

Description: vCPU, memory and storage allocated
Informs design decision: Hub capacity per application
Caveats: Provisioned only; performance sizing belongs to the infrastructure team

Description: USB dongles, serial ports, passthrough devices
Informs design decision: Exception list: workloads tied to site hardware
Source detail: VM hardware configuration (USB, serial, PCI passthrough)
Secondary or cross-check source: App owner; site survey for physical servers
Caveats: Dongles on physical servers need the owner or a site check

Description: Whether the host is running and when it last reported
Informs design decision: Separates retired hosts from DR or period-end hosts
Caveats: Powered off does not mean unused

Description: Whether the host reports to Defender
Informs design decision: Coverage gap list; which hosts need other sources
Caveats: Unmatched VMs are a finding in themselves

Description: Which domain controllers have a healthy sensor
Informs design decision: Whether authentication evidence is complete for each site
Secondary or cross-check source: Domain controller list from RunZero, Netbox or the identity team
Caveats: Any DC without a sensor is a silent gap in every authentication field

Description: Executable or service providing the component
Informs design decision: Identifies application components on each host
Secondary or cross-check source: Aria Service Discovery (Type) for hosts not onboarded
Caveats: Onboarded devices only

Description: Where the component is installed and its version
Informs design decision: Separates instances; version exceptions
Caveats: None

Description: TCP and UDP ports each component listens on
Informs design decision: Hub access rules; join key to user evidence
Source detail: DeviceNetworkEvents: LocalPort, Protocol on listening and inbound events
Secondary or cross-check source: RunZero open-port scan; Aria Service Discovery (Ports)
Caveats: Listener events may be recorded only when the listener opens; test against a long-running server

Description: Components using ephemeral or RPC-assigned ports
Informs design decision: Whether port-based rules or matching will work
Source detail: From Defender ports in the ephemeral range or RPC processes
Caveats: Match on process, not port

Description: Web, application, database, file or middleware
Informs design decision: Which components must move together
Caveats: Confirm with the technical owner

Description: Account the component runs as
Informs design decision: Identity dependencies; credential changes at migration
Source detail: DeviceProcessEvents: AccountName, AccountDomain for the service process
Caveats: None

Description: SMB shares served from the host and who uses them
Informs design decision: File service consolidation design
Source detail: Client-side DeviceNetworkEvents to RemotePort 445 (gives user and client)
Secondary or cross-check source: Splunk Windows Security 5140 and 5145 if auditing is enabled; RunZero SMB discovery
Caveats: Share names need Splunk audit events or a host query

Description: Subject and SAN names on certificates the service presents
Informs design decision: FQDNs the app is published under; certificate reissue at migration
Caveats: SAN names often reveal FQDNs missing from DNS evidence

Description: DNS names clients use to reach the application
Informs design decision: DNS changes and certificate scope when the app moves
Source detail: Client-side DeviceNetworkEvents: RemoteUrl for connections to the server IP
Secondary or cross-check source: Splunk DNS query logs if ingested; Netbox DNS name; RunZero certificate SAN
Caveats: RemoteUrl is not populated for every connection

Description: Clients connecting directly to the IP address
Informs design decision: Exception list: hard-coded addresses break when the server moves
Source detail: Client-side DeviceNetworkEvents to the server IP with empty RemoteUrl
Secondary or cross-check source: Splunk DNS logs showing no lookup
Caveats: An empty RemoteUrl can also be missing data; corroborate before listing

Description: Browser, thick client, RDP or Citrix, file share, API
Informs design decision: Client delivery model from the hub (latency, VDI)
Caveats: None

Description: HTTP(S), SMB, RDP, SQL, LDAP or other
Informs design decision: Latency tolerance and WAN suitability
Secondary or cross-check source: Inferred from Defender ports and process
Caveats: Non-standard ports need fingerprinting

Description: SMBv1, NTLMv1, cleartext LDAP, Telnet, FTP
Informs design decision: Exception list: protocols that may not work through the hub design
Secondary or cross-check source: Defender for Identity IdentityLogonEvents (Protocol; LDAP cleartext logon type); Defender ports
Caveats: None

Description: Posts and data centres users connect from
Informs design decision: Hub placement and WAN capacity
Secondary or cross-check source: Defender IdentityInfo City and Country (user's home location)
Caveats: Roaming and remote users skew site counts

Description: Direct, ZPA, VPN or Citrix
Informs design decision: Access design after consolidation
Caveats: ZPA rollout incomplete; behind ZPA the server sees the App Connector IP, not the client

Description: Load balancers, reverse proxies, Citrix or RDS in front of the app
Informs design decision: Where users are visible; what moves with the app
Secondary or cross-check source: Defender: many users arriving from one source IP; Netbox VIP records
Caveats: Outside application analysis scope; owned by the network team

Description: Whether the app is reachable from the internet
Informs design decision: Security footprint; publishing design at the hub
Caveats: Not a full exposure assessment

Description: Whether the app tolerates WAN latency to a hub
Informs design decision: Whether the app can be served from a regional hub
Caveats: SMB and SQL from thick clients are the main risk; test before deciding

Description: Bytes and connection rates per application
Informs design decision: WAN sizing to the hub
Caveats: No flow data in scope; Defender has no byte counts

Description: Kerberos, NTLM, LDAP bind, SAML or OIDC, local or forms, certificate
Informs design decision: Identity design at the hub; exception list for local or legacy auth
Secondary or cross-check source: Entra sign-in events for SSO apps; Splunk IIS and app logs; app owner
Caveats: Covers only DCs with a sensor (HST-15). No AD or Entra evidence suggests local or forms auth; confirm with owner

Description: AD domain or forest, or Entra tenant, the app trusts
Informs design decision: Trust and identity boundary design
Caveats: Cross-domain trusts are boundary risks; domains whose DCs lack sensors are missing (HST-15)

Description: Which DC the server and its users authenticate against
Informs design decision: Whether removing a post DC breaks the app
Source detail: IdentityLogonEvents: DC that processed the logon
Secondary or cross-check source: Splunk DC events 4624 and 4769; Defender DeviceNetworkEvents to ports 88, 389, 636
Caveats: Apps pinned to a local DC fail silently when it is removed; a post DC without a sensor shows no logons (HST-15)

Description: SPNs and delegation settings for the app's service account
Informs design decision: SPN and delegation changes when hostnames change
Secondary or cross-check source: Defender for Identity (logon events; Kerberos delegation posture assessment); directory query by identity team
Caveats: Delegation settings need a directory query

Description: Credentials in config files, scripts or command lines
Informs design decision: Exception list: credential changes required at migration
Caveats: Tools cannot detect this reliably; treat as a risk to test per app

Description: Who uses the application
Informs design decision: User impact, test cohorts, cutover communication
Source detail: Client-side DeviceNetworkEvents: InitiatingProcessAccountUpn to server IP and port
Secondary or cross-check source: Defender for Identity IdentityLogonEvents.AccountUpn; Splunk 4624 logon type 3; ZPA user
Caveats: Back-end tiers show service accounts only; Citrix and proxies hide users

Description: How many users and which areas
Informs design decision: Prioritisation and stakeholder engagement
Caveats: Count depends on the observation window; always state it

Description: Calls from each component to other components and apps
Informs design decision: Move groups: what must move together
Secondary or cross-check source: Aria Service Discovery relationships; RunZero for endpoints not onboarded
Caveats: Process is visible only on onboarded ends

Description: DNS, DHCP, NTP, AD, print, SMTP relay, PKI, file shares at the post
Informs design decision: Which post services must be replicated or replaced at the hub
Secondary or cross-check source: Netbox service IPs per site; RunZero
Caveats: Hard-coded resolver and relay IPs are common exceptions

Description: Vendor APIs, SFTP, partner links, cloud services
Informs design decision: Egress and partner allow-list changes at the hub
Source detail: Server-side DeviceNetworkEvents with public RemoteIP or RemoteUrl
Secondary or cross-check source: Zscaler ZIA logs if server traffic is forwarded
Caveats: Partners that allow-list a post's public IP break silently when egress moves

Description: Jobs that run on a schedule
Informs design decision: Exception list: jobs to reschedule or re-point
Source detail: Task Scheduler, Security 4698 and cron logs if ingested
Secondary or cross-check source: Defender DeviceProcessEvents (children of the scheduler); DeviceEvents ScheduledTaskCreated
Caveats: Defender's 30-day window misses monthly and annual jobs

Description: Month-end, quarter-end and EOFY activity
Informs design decision: Cutover timing; exception list
Source detail: Activity across at least one period-end (longest retention)
Secondary or cross-check source: App owner confirmation; repeat Defender and VMware extracts after month-end
Caveats: EOFY jobs need 12 months of history or owner confirmation

Description: Most recent client connection
Informs design decision: Retire or migrate
Source detail: Latest client-side connection timestamp to server IP and port
Caveats: No use in 30 days does not prove unused

Description: Manual steps users or IT perform around the app
Informs design decision: Exception list; process changes needed
Caveats: Not observable by tools

Description: Sensitivity of the data the app holds
Informs design decision: Security controls at the hub
Caveats: None

Description: Legal or policy limits on where data can be hosted
Informs design decision: Whether the app can move to a hub in another country
Caveats: Most likely blocker for cross-border hubs; confirm early

Description: Licences tied to host, site, IP, MAC or hardware dongle
Informs design decision: Whether relocation needs vendor approval or relicensing
Caveats: MAC- or IP-bound licences fail silently after a move

Description: Observed, inferred or stakeholder
Informs design decision: Confidence in each design input
Caveats: Never let an inferred value pass as observed

Description: Tool, query and date range each value came from, with extract time zone
Informs design decision: Whether a gap is real or an artefact of the window
Caveats: A 7-day sample is a 7-day observation
